$comment: The right workflow with a reason that would fit any intent at all. This is the case that says route accuracy
on its own is not enough: a router that happens to be right and cannot say why is indistinguishable, on the
menu code alone, from one that read the message.
A frozen copy of one case of the live corpus, of the menu it is scored against, and of the user's message.
Those three plus the reply are the whole input to scoreCase, so all three are stored here rather than read
live: a replay has to keep scoring the scenario it was derived against after the corpus moves on, and
npm run test:eval-routing-data already holds the live corpus against the shipped menu.

expected.rationale: The implementation is shipped, so tests are written against it rather than ahead of it. This is the mirror of the ATDD case, and `already built` against that case's `failing` is the pair that separates them.

inputs.intent: The checkout service is already built and shipped behind a flag. It has no API tests at all. Generate a prioritized set for it.

derivation: route/TA/bmad-testarch-automate is what the oracle expects, so actionCorrect, menuCorrect, workflowCorrect and
decidingTokens is [api test, already built]. The reason carries neither, so tokensFound is 0 and tokensMissed
names both. That is the whole point of the case: the score for the decision and the score for the stated reason
scopeTokens is [checkout] and the scope reads "the checkout service", well inside the bound, so scopeOk is true.

answer.reason: this is the right workflow for what you are asking about
